purpose: Seat workspace design alternatives for review; not implemented

variants.name: 01-shared-bench
variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a polished raster design concept for the seat-selection map of Cleany, a commercial office robot dashboard. Landscape 1536x1024. This image is a close-up of ONE office desk cluster, not a full dashboard. Perfectly orthographic top-down plan, no isometric perspective. White canvas, restrained slate-blue outlines, very pale cool gray surfaces, teal #00636d for selected workspace. Large clear main drawing centered, generous margins, small understated title at top left. Six real working positions: three along the top side facing downward, three along the bottom facing upward. Top positions numbered 01, 02, 03 left to right; bottom positions 09, 10, 11 left to right. Put these identifiers ON THE DESKTOP in their own personal work area, never on chairs and never in detached floating square buttons. Six smaller UNNUMBERED office chairs outside the desk edges, each recognizable as a seat cushion with a curved back and short side supports, facing its desk. Emphasize the difference between a personal desk area and the chair. Select top-middle workspace 02 in teal while keeping its number highly legible. Consistent clean interface typography, crisp scalable-looking geometry, no people, no photo textures, no decorative plants, no navigation, no task panel, no extra labels, no badges on chairs, no watermark. This is one variant only, not a comparison collage.
Title text exactly: "01 / SHARED BENCH". Design: ONE continuous long rectangular shared desk with gently rounded outer corners. A thin horizontal divider separates the two facing rows, and thin vertical seams split each row into three equal personal desktop zones. The six zones are parts of a single tabletop, not six loose cards. Put large plain seat numbers directly in the center of each zone. No monitors or keyboards. Selected 02 fills the entire top-middle desktop zone with very pale teal, with a crisp teal outline confined to that workspace; its number is dark teal. All six chairs remain small neutral outlines, detached from desk by a natural clearance. The visual meaning should be six people sharing a bench, each with their own numbered surface.

Title text exactly: "02 / DESK MODULES". Design: SIX distinct individual rectangular desk surfaces organized as two facing rows of three desks, with narrow clear white gaps between adjacent desktop modules and a slim central shared partition. Each desktop has a tiny unnumbered monitor and keyboard icon near the center partition, oriented toward the person sitting there; the number is printed clearly at the outer front corner of that DESK, readable upright for the viewer. Small ergonomic office chairs outside the desks make each workstation unmistakable. Selected top-middle 02 desktop has a muted teal surface, white number and pale simple monitor glyph. The other desktops are near white with slate outlines. This must visibly read as separate modular office workstations, not one shared table or a grid of UI buttons.

Title text exactly: "03 / PERSONAL WORK AREAS". Design: ONE broad continuous rounded shared tabletop, WITHOUT physical divider lines or partitions. Define each person's usable work surface through SIX large subtle rounded desk mats inset on the tabletop, three per side. Each mat has a tiny abstract keyboard rectangle oriented toward its chair, and a small clear seat number printed directly on its front edge, never in a separate pill. Selected top-middle mat 02 is a generous pale teal translucent workspace area with a thin teal boundary and dark teal number; the surrounding tabletop remains light gray. Keep substantial visible tabletop between mats so these read as personal desk work areas rather than floating buttons. Six compact neutral chairs positioned outside the table, visibly smaller than the work surfaces. Soft, slightly warmer light gray desk tone than the other concepts, still crisp flat professional mapping style, no 3D.
